title: pinout-asyncapi compatibility report (output DTO)
description: Machine-readable JSON report emitted on stdout (and, when settings.save_json_report, to settings.json_report_file) by `pinout-asyncapi validate`. Consumed by pinout-netlist for aggregation. Conforms to the ecosystem report canon 1.1 (source of truth: pinout-openapi/docs/report-format.md); mirrors the sync twin pinout-openapi/api-specification/report.schema.json with exactly two differences — the async `errors[].code` enum (rules R1-R9) and `uncovered_channels[]` in place of `uncovered_operations[]`. The process EXIT CODE (separate from this document) is fixed in x-exit-codes below. FROZEN: this is the sole output contract of the service.
x-canon: pinout-openapi/docs/report-format.md (canon 1.1; owner epic E1). Canon 1.1 is an ADDITIVE superset of the flat form both validators actually froze under 1.0: it adds validator / interaction / consumer / generated_at / errors[].subject, and declares `provenance` the single source of provider identity (no separate provider{} block). Decision record: pinout/debt/report-canon-fork.md (operator, variant A, 2026-07-25).

x-exit-codes.description: Canonical Result->exit mapping, aligned with the sync twin. The exit code is the CLI's status line — the machine-readable serialization of the outcome; it is NOT a field of this report document. CONFIG_ERROR (exit 2) is a config-side breach detected before a report is written, so it never appears in errors[].code.

table.meaning: a verdict: the domain honestly said no (contract broken)
bad invocation / unreadable / schema-invalid config, or provider spec source not exactly-one
environment/spec: io or parse failure of an input artifact (consumed-contract or provider spec)

schema_version.description: Report-canon semver. 1.1 is additive over the 1.0 flat form; pinout-netlist reads sync and async reports with one reader.

validator.description: Which validator produced the report. Build-time constant. Canon enum is `pinout-openapi | pinout-asyncapi`; this contract pins the async member.

interaction.description: Interaction style of the checked pair, so pinout-netlist can label the edge without guessing. Build-time constant. Canon enum is `sync | async`; this contract pins `async`.

consumer.description: Consumer identity. Without it pinout-netlist cannot build a consumer->provider edge — it would know the provider (from provenance) but not who depends on it.

name.description: Consumer service name, taken from config.consumer.name (config.schema.json).

version.description: Consumer version. OPTIONAL and emitted only when actually known — there is no source for it in the MVP input contracts, so it is normally absent. Never emit a placeholder.

generated_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of report generation; pinout-netlist uses it as the freshness `at` of the verdict record. INJECTED FROM ABOVE through a clock port — never read from the system clock inside the core, otherwise component tests become non-deterministic (see docs/concept.md D10).

compatible.description: Aggregate verdict. Invariant: compatible <=> errors == []. true => exit 0; false => exit 1.

provenance.description: Which provider spec the consumer's contract was captured from — echoed from the consumed-contract stamp. Canon 1.1 declares this the SINGLE source of provider identity: there is deliberately no separate provider{} block, because provenance is strictly stronger (it carries the capture hash, so netlist can track freshness and re-check on provider change).

provider.description: Provider name as stamped at capture time.

provider_version.description: Version stamp of the source spec (AsyncAPI info.version or the commit that produced it).

captured_hash.description: sha256:... hash of the captured provider spec bytes.

errors.description: All violations folded across channels and directions (verdict codes R1-R9 at exit 1) and any input-side io/parse breach that produced a report (exit 3). No rule short-circuits, so one run can surface several. Empty <=> compatible.

code.description: Stable traceability key (TASK <-> use-case <-> contract <-> test). Verdict codes: CHANNEL_NOT_IN_PROVIDER (R1), PROTOCOL_MISMATCH (R2), DIRECTION_NOT_IN_PROVIDER (R3), MESSAGE_NOT_IN_PROVIDER (R4), MISSING_REQUIRED_SENT_FIELD (R5), READS_FIELD_NOT_PROVIDED (R6), TYPE_MISMATCH (R7), CONTENT_TYPE_MISMATCH (R8), CORRELATION_ID_MISMATCH (R9) -> exit 1. Io/parse codes: PARSE_ERROR, FILE_NOT_FOUND, HTTP_ERROR, TIMEOUT_ERROR -> exit 3. See x-exit-codes.
code.x-async-subject-note: Verdict codes carry a channel-scoped subject; io/parse codes carry an artifact-scoped subject. See `subject`.

subject.description: What the violation is ABOUT — the graph-edge granularity pinout-netlist keys on (one subject = one edge). For verdict codes (R1-R9) it is the async subject `<channel address>` plus, when known, ` <direction> <message key>` — e.g. `WALLET.BALANCE.RESPONSE receive getBalanceResponse`. For io/parse codes there is no channel, so the subject is the input artifact that failed — e.g. the provider spec_url/spec_path or the consumed-contract path. IMPLEMENTATION RULE: subject is the PREFIX of `location`, extracted from one computation, never composed a second time by hand (docs/concept.md D11).

location.description: The full `at` of the violation: `subject` plus the dotted field path when applicable, e.g. `WALLET.BALANCE.RESPONSE receive getBalanceResponse payload.data.balance`. The message key is the channel `messages` map key, never the parsed Message.Name (see docs/concept.md D8). Direction is `send` or `receive` as seen FROM THE CONSUMER.

details.description: Detail (expected vs actual type, field name, protocol pair).

uncovered_channels.description: Informational only: provider channel addresses outside consumer.channels. No effect on the verdict or the exit code. Async counterpart of the twin's uncovered_operations[]; deliberately NOT renamed — the async subject is a channel.
